# security-testing

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D8 QA & Testing (QA)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** integration-testing, e2e-testing
- **Feeds into:** qa-gates, bug-triage

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** A release needs security evidence: WSTG checklist execution, CI scanner triage, authorization/IDOR testing, session and authentication abuse cases — always against the project's own staging or production-like environments, or inside its own CI pipeline.
- **Do NOT use when:** The target is any system the project does not own or operate — never in scope, no exceptions. Tool selection, hardening, and fixes belong to D7 (security); penetration testing under a written engagement belongs to D7's penetration-testing skill.

## Rules

1. **QA-181 — Written scope before any test runs.** The test plan names the target environments (own staging/production-like only), the accounts and roles used, and the techniques allowed; testing outside that written scope does not start.
2. **QA-182 — WSTG checklist per release.** Each release executes the app-relevant OWASP WSTG categories (information gathering, authentication, authorization, session management, input validation, business logic) under their stable test IDs (e.g., WSTG-INFO-05), with pass/fail and evidence recorded per case.
3. **QA-183 — Skipped categories are named, with reasons.** The release record lists every WSTG category executed and every category skipped with its reason; an unlisted category is treated as not executed.
4. **QA-184 — Scanner suite in CI on every change.** Dependency, SAST, secrets, and container/config scanners run on every change; a new confirmed critical or high finding fails the pipeline with a non-zero exit.
5. **QA-185 — Every scanner result is triaged.** Each result is marked confirmed-exploitable, accepted-risk with a written note, or false-positive with the reason; raw scanner output is never the finding record.
6. **QA-186 — Authorization matrix by replay.** For every privileged endpoint, an automated test replays the request with a lower-privilege session and requires rejection (401/403); UI hiding is never accepted as evidence of enforcement.
7. **QA-187 — IDOR sweep on object access.** For every endpoint that takes an object ID, a test requests another account's object ID under a different session and requires rejection, run against own staging data only.
8. **QA-188 — Session cases per the OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet.** Tests verify cookie flags (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite), session rotation on login and privilege change, and server-side invalidation on logout.
9. **QA-189 — Authentication abuse cases pass end to end.** A wrong password is rejected (no any-password login), and a password reset is proven by logging in with the new password while the old one fails — receiving the reset email alone is not a pass.
10. **QA-190 — Findings close only by retest.** Every finding is recorded with evidence, severity, and remediation, and is retested after the fix; an unretested fix leaves the finding open.
11. **QA-191 — Business-logic abuse cases per release.** The app's core flows get manual abuse cases scanners cannot see: price/quantity tampering, step skipping, replayed submissions, and concurrent-request races, each with a recorded verdict.
12. **QA-192 — DAST only against own staging, authenticated.** Dynamic scans run against the project's staging environment with test accounts for each role; results enter the same triage queue as every other scanner (QA-185).

## BAN list

- **BAN-QA-091 — Cosmetic authorization accepted as tested.** Banned: signing off authorization because a privileged button is hidden in the UI while the endpoint was never replay-tested. Defeats: DET-FAKE-021. Instead: replay the delete request with a standard-user session and require 403 before sign-off (QA-186). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-092 — Reset test that stops at the email.** Banned: marking password reset tested because a reset email arrived, without proving the credential changed. Defeats: DET-FAKE-020. Instead: complete the reset, then assert login with the old password fails and login with the new password succeeds (QA-189). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-093 — Security control disabled to get CI green.** Banned: suppressing a scanner rule, skipping the secrets scan, or loosening an auth check in shipped configuration so the pipeline passes. Defeats: DET-CODE-020. Instead: fix the finding, or record an accepted-risk note with owner and expiry and keep the control on (QA-185). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-094 — Session "verified" by a client-side flag.** Banned: treating a `loggedIn=true` value in browser storage as proof a session exists or is enforced. Defeats: DET-FAKE-002. Instead: verify the server-issued session cookie's flags and that a protected API call without it is rejected (QA-188). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-095 — Real credentials hardcoded in test assets.** Banned: real passwords, tokens, or API keys committed in security-test fixtures, scripts, or CI configuration. Defeats: DET-CODE-018. Instead: use dedicated staging test accounts whose credentials live in the CI secret store and are injected at runtime. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-QA-091 — Scanner gate.** Verifies: QA-184, QA-185. Check: `scripts/security-scan.sh` runs the dependency, SAST, secrets, and container/config scanners and exits non-zero on any new confirmed critical/high finding. Pass: exit code 0 and a triage record exists for every result. Fail: block merge/release.
- **G-QA-092 — Authorization matrix gate.** Verifies: QA-186, QA-187. Check: `npm run test:authz` runs the privilege-replay and IDOR suites; the run exits non-zero if any privileged endpoint lacks a replay test or any replay is not rejected. Pass: exit code 0 with one replay test per privileged endpoint. Fail: block release.
- **G-QA-093 — Seeded-fault negative control.** Verifies: QA-184. Check: on a scratch branch, seed one known-vulnerable dependency and remove one authorization check, then run the pipeline; both G-QA-091 and G-QA-092 must exit non-zero. Pass: both gates report red on the seeded branch. Fail: the gates are broken — fix the gates before any release relies on them.
- **G-QA-094 — WSTG release record gate.** Verifies: QA-182, QA-183. Check: `test -s docs/security/wstg-record.md && grep -q "Skipped:" docs/security/wstg-record.md` — the record exists, names executed categories by WSTG ID with evidence, and lists skipped categories with reasons. Pass: command exits 0. Fail: block release sign-off.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Written scope names own environments, accounts, and allowed techniques (QA-181).
- [ ] WSTG record lists executed categories by ID with evidence, and skipped categories with reasons (QA-182, QA-183).
- [ ] Scanner suite ran in CI on this change and exited 0 (QA-184, G-QA-091).
- [ ] Every scanner result carries a triage verdict (QA-185).
- [ ] Privilege-replay and IDOR suites pass, one replay per privileged endpoint (QA-186, QA-187, G-QA-092).
- [ ] Session cases cover cookie flags, rotation, and logout invalidation (QA-188).
- [ ] Reset proven by login with the new password; wrong-password login rejected (QA-189).
- [ ] All fixed findings retested; seeded-fault control still turns the gates red (QA-190, G-QA-093).

# test-data

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D8 QA & Testing (QA)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** test-strategy
- **Feeds into:** qa-gates, placeholder-scan, e2e-testing, integration-testing

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** creating, reviewing, or fixing the data any test, seed script, fixture, or demo environment runs on — factories, builders, fixtures, seed scripts, test database lifecycle, or production-shaped data requests.
- **Do NOT use when:** designing production seed/reference data itself (countries, plans, tax tables as shipped product data) — use seed-data (D5); or deciding data retention and privacy policy — use D14's privacy skills. This skill governs data manufactured for testing and demos.

## Rules

1. **QA-241 — Manufactured, never harvested.** All test data is created by code — factories, builders, or fixtures versioned with the tests that use them. No test data originates from a database export, a spreadsheet, or a manual insert.
2. **QA-242 — Tests own their data.** A test reads only data it created or explicitly loaded in its own setup. Shared mutable fixtures that tests read and write are prohibited; order dependence traced to shared data is a defect in the fixture, not in the test order.
3. **QA-243 — Valid by default.** A factory call with zero overrides produces a record that passes every validation and constraint of the real model. If a legal record needs overrides, fix the factory defaults, not the call sites.
4. **QA-244 — Deterministic generation.** Every random-looking value comes from a seeded generator whose seed is fixed in the repo or logged by the run. Wall-clock time is never read directly: dates and timestamps are computed relative to an injected clock.
5. **QA-245 — The harness owns the lifecycle.** The test database is created by the project's migrations, populated per test or per suite, and destroyed or reset by the harness afterward. No test depends on rows left behind by a previous run, and no cleanup is done by hand.
6. **QA-246 — Synthetic data is labeled synthetic, end to end.** Every seed or fixture record carries a machine-readable marker (for example an `is_seed` flag or a reserved seed email domain) that survives into API responses and screens in non-production environments. Generated people and records are never presented as real users, customers, or activity.
7. **QA-247 — The seed path refuses production.** The seed entry point checks the environment before writing anything and exits non-zero when the environment is production, unless an explicit demo flag is set — and demo-flagged seeding still writes only marker-carrying records (QA-246).
8. **QA-248 — No production data in test environments.** Production rows are never copied into test, CI, staging, or development databases — including "anonymized" copies that keep real names, emails, or phone numbers. When production shape is needed, generate the same shape synthetically; any exception is sanitized under D14's privacy rules before it leaves production.
9. **QA-249 — Fixtures contain no real personal details.** Fixture people are invented: names created for the fixture, email addresses on reserved domains (`example.com`, `example.org`), phone numbers from reserved fictional ranges. A real person's details in a fixture file are a privacy defect, not a convenience.
10. **QA-250 — Reference data comes from the shared fixtures.** Countries, plans, currencies, and other shared reference data are loaded from the same fixtures development uses. Test-local copies that can drift from the shared set are prohibited.

## BAN list

- **BAN-QA-121 — Production database copy as test data.** Banned: restoring a production dump (full or partial) into any test, CI, staging, or development database. Defeats: DET-FAKE-014. Instead: generate production-shaped synthetic data with factories at comparable volume, or sanitize under D14's privacy rules before any non-production use. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-122 — Seed users shipped as real customers.** Banned: seed or fixture accounts, testimonials, or activity presented in production as real users or social proof. Defeats: DET-FAKE-014. Instead: keep seed accounts in development and demo environments only, behind the QA-247 environment guard, marker-carrying, and excluded from the production seed path. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-123 — Real personal details in fixtures.** Banned: real names paired with real email addresses, phone numbers, or other personal details of real people anywhere in fixture or seed files. Defeats: DET-FAKE-014. Instead: invent fixture people with `example.com` addresses and reserved fictional phone numbers (QA-249). Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-124 — Identical staged notifications for every account.** Banned: seeding every account with the same pre-written notification or activity feed presented as real events. Defeats: DET-FAKE-013. Instead: generate notifications from real events inside the test; fresh accounts start with an empty feed, and demo notifications are labeled demo data. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-QA-121 — Isolation proof.** Verifies: QA-242, QA-245. Check: in CI, run the full suite with randomized test order, then run each test file standalone (the framework's shuffle and per-file modes). Pass: both runs fully green. Fail: block merge; the failing test's data dependencies are fixed, not reordered.
- **G-QA-122 — Seed/production refusal check.** Verifies: QA-247. Check: invoke the project's seed command with production environment variables set (for example `APP_ENV=production npm run db:seed`, substituting the project's actual command). Pass: the command exits non-zero and writes zero rows. Fail: block release until the guard exists.
- **G-QA-123 — Fixture personal-data scan.** Verifies: QA-246, QA-249. Check: run the placeholder-scan sweep over fixture and seed directories, including `grep -rEi '@(gmail|yahoo|hotmail|outlook|icloud)\.com' tests/ fixtures/ db/` plus a marker audit of every fixture user record. Pass: zero real-domain hits and every fixture user carries the synthetic marker. Fail: block merge; replace the data, do not allow-list it.
- **G-QA-124 — Determinism check.** Verifies: QA-244. Check: run the data-generating test files twice with the fixed seed and diff the generated fixture snapshots or database dumps between runs. Pass: byte-identical output. Fail: block merge until the unseeded source is seeded or clock-injected.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] All test data is produced by factories, builders, or fixtures versioned with the tests (QA-241).
- [ ] The full suite passes with randomized order and per-file standalone runs (G-QA-121).
- [ ] Factories produce valid records with zero overrides (QA-243).
- [ ] Generators are seeded and time comes from an injected clock (QA-244).
- [ ] Every seed/fixture record carries the synthetic marker (QA-246).
- [ ] The seed command exits non-zero under production environment variables (G-QA-122).
- [ ] No production rows and no real personal details exist in any fixture or seed file (QA-248, QA-249, G-QA-123).

# test-strategy

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D8 QA & Testing (QA)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** none (consumes the project's acceptance criteria from D1)
- **Feeds into:** unit-testing, integration-testing, e2e-testing, browser-verification, visual-regression, accessibility-testing, load-testing, chaos-testing, contract-testing, security-testing, qa-gates, test-data, bug-triage, placeholder-scan

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** starting a project, before any test suite is written; when the architecture changes materially; when a new test type is proposed; at each release, for the strategy-to-suite audit.
- **Do NOT use when:** writing or fixing an individual suite (use that layer's skill, executing against this strategy); setting merge-gate wiring or thresholds (qa-gates — this skill decides what must be proven, qa-gates wires the proof into CI).

## Rules

1. **QA-201 — One strategy document.** The strategy lives in TESTING.md at the repo root, is committed before the suites grow, and is the single place that names layers, environments, and budgets; a strategy that lives in a slide deck, wiki, or chat thread does not exist.
2. **QA-202 — Pyramid allocation in numbers.** TESTING.md states the target count or share per layer (unit / integration / e2e) and a wall-clock runtime budget per layer; "mostly unit tests" without numbers fails this rule.
3. **QA-203 — Every acceptance class maps to a layer.** Each requirement class in the project's acceptance criteria names at least one test layer that can catch its failure; a class with no layer is moved to the Accepted Risks section (QA-204), never left unmapped.
4. **QA-204 — Exclusions are written, with reasons.** TESTING.md carries an explicit Not Tested / Accepted Risks section: each entry names what is not tested, why, and who accepted the risk; silence is a gap, a written exclusion is a decision.
5. **QA-205 — E2E admission is earned.** A flow earns an e2e test by revenue or risk (signup, login, the core transaction, the top admin action); the PR adding one names the lower layer that cannot cover the case, or the test is pushed down the pyramid.
6. **QA-206 — Quality attributes are assigned, not assumed.** Visual, accessibility, load, chaos, contract, and security testing each appear in TESTING.md with an owning D8 skill, the environment they run in, and their cadence (per-PR, nightly, per-release); an attribute with no owner is untested by definition.
7. **QA-207 — Environment and cadence matrix.** TESTING.md states where each layer runs — local, CI per-PR, merge/nightly, or release pipeline; expensive gates (full-browser e2e, load, chaos) are scheduled explicitly, and "nightly" entries name the job that runs them so they cannot silently become "never."
8. **QA-208 — Flake budget is a number.** TESTING.md sets a maximum flake rate per suite; a flaky test is quarantined only as a tracked state with a named owner and an expiry date recorded in the strategy's quarantine list.
9. **QA-209 — Thresholds trace to a source document.** Every numeric threshold in the strategy (latency percentiles, error rates, Core Web Vitals budgets) cites the budget or SLO document it comes from; loosening a threshold is a reviewed change to that source document, never an edit inside a test PR.
10. **QA-210 — Every suite has a named owner.** TESTING.md lists each suite with its owning skill; a suite with no owner is adopted or deleted at the next strategy review — unowned suites are not run and not reported.
11. **QA-211 — New test types enter the strategy first.** A new kind of testing is added to TESTING.md (layer, budget, owner, cadence) in a reviewed change before its first test lands in the repo.
12. **QA-212 — Fake-functionality coverage is mapped.** For every interactive feature class in the DET-FAKE family (auth, payments, uploads, forms, counters, exports), TESTING.md names which skill runs its persistence and network probe — placeholder-scan, browser-verification, or e2e-testing — so no claimed effect goes unprobed.

## BAN list

- **BAN-QA-101 — Deck-only strategy.** Banned: presenting a strategy deck or document as the project's verification while no committed TESTING.md or running suites stand behind it. Defeats: DET-FAKE-022. Instead: write TESTING.md with layers, budgets, and owners, and land the first suite it names before claiming any coverage. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-102 — Coverage percentage as proof.** Banned: reporting a coverage number (or a green dashboard) as evidence the product works, when the tests behind it assert nothing. Defeats: DET-CODE-012. Instead: pair every coverage claim with the layer census (G-QA-102) and seeded-fault evidence that the suites can fail. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-103 — Staged-account verification claimed as coverage.** Banned: counting manual click-throughs on a curated demo account as test coverage for a flow. Defeats: DET-FAKE-014. Instead: cover the flow with an isolated automated journey that provisions its own account and data (e2e-testing), and record the demo pass as exploratory only. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-104 — Unnumbered budgets.** Banned: strategy language like "keep e2e small" or "suites stay fast" with no counts, runtimes, or flake ceiling. Defeats: DET-FAKE-005. Instead: state the e2e count ceiling, per-layer runtime budgets, and flake ceiling as numbers the census gate can check. Severity: WARN.

## Gates

- **G-QA-101 — Strategy document and mapping audit.** Verifies: QA-201, QA-203. Check: `test -f TESTING.md && python3 scripts/qa/check_strategy_map.py` — the script exits non-zero if TESTING.md is missing, contains TODO/TBD placeholders, or any acceptance-criteria class lacks a named layer or an Accepted Risks entry. Pass: exit 0. Fail: block the release; fix the map or record the risk.
- **G-QA-102 — Layer census within budgets.** Verifies: QA-202, QA-205, QA-210. Check: CI runs `node scripts/qa/layer-census.mjs --budgets TESTING.md --fail-on-breach`; it counts tests and wall time per layer and exits non-zero when a count, runtime, or unowned suite breaches the strategy. Pass: exit 0. Fail: block merge; push tests down the pyramid, adopt, or delete.
- **G-QA-103 — Accepted risks are explicit.** Verifies: QA-204. Check: `python3 scripts/qa/check_risks.py` exits non-zero if the Accepted Risks section is absent, empty, or any entry lacks a reason or a named acceptor. Pass: exit 0. Fail: block the release until every exclusion is written and owned.
- **G-QA-104 — Flake budget and quarantine hygiene.** Verifies: QA-208. Check: `python3 scripts/qa/flake_report.py --max-rate 0.02` exits non-zero when a suite's measured flake rate exceeds the TESTING.md ceiling or any quarantined test lacks an owner or a future expiry date. Pass: exit 0. Fail: block the release; fix, extend with justification, or delete the flaky test.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] TESTING.md exists at the repo root and predates the suites it governs (QA-201).
- [ ] Per-layer counts/shares and runtime budgets are stated as numbers (QA-202).
- [ ] Every acceptance-criteria class maps to a named layer or an Accepted Risks entry (QA-203, QA-204).
- [ ] Visual, accessibility, load, chaos, contract, and security each have an owner, environment, and cadence (QA-206).
- [ ] Each layer's environment and cadence are named, including the nightly job names (QA-207).
- [ ] Flake ceiling is set and every quarantined test has an owner and expiry (QA-208).
- [ ] Every threshold cites its source budget/SLO document (QA-209).
- [ ] DET-FAKE probe ownership is mapped for every interactive feature class (QA-212).

# unit-testing

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D8 QA & Testing (QA)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** test-strategy
- **Feeds into:** qa-gates, integration-testing

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** writing or reviewing tests for a single module, function, or class — pricing math, validation, parsing, state transitions, permission checks — that can be proven without a database, network, or browser.
- **Do NOT use when:** the behavior only exists across real collaborators (database, HTTP layer, another service) — use integration-testing; or across a full user journey — use e2e-testing. Do not stretch a unit test into either by mocking the collaborators away.

## Rules

1. **QA-001 — One test file per module, fast runner, first job.** Each module has a matching test file run by the stack's fast runner (Vitest, pytest, JUnit); the unit suite is the first CI job and finishes within the wall-time budget in TESTING.md.
2. **QA-002 — Every test asserts a specific expected value.** A test states the exact output, state, or side effect it expects. A test whose only assertion is "does not throw" is labeled a smoke test and never counts toward coverage of logic.
3. **QA-003 — Tests are isolated and order-independent.** Each test arranges its own inputs; no shared mutable fixtures, no reliance on another test's leftovers. The suite passes with tests shuffled and with any single test run alone.
4. **QA-004 — No real network, database, filesystem, or wall-clock.** Time and randomness are injected as parameters or fakes controlled by the test; a unit test that sleeps, reads the real clock, or opens a socket is defective.
5. **QA-005 — Assert behavior, not implementation.** Assert on return values and observable side effects, never on private internals or call-by-call mock choreography that a behavior-preserving refactor would break.
6. **QA-006 — Doubles live at the unit boundary only.** External collaborators (payment API, email sender) may be replaced by test doubles; the unit under test and the project's own modules are never doubled.
7. **QA-007 — A bug fix lands with its failing test.** The regression test is written first or in the same commit as the fix, so the bug is permanently pinned; a fix with no test is incomplete work.
8. **QA-008 — Coverage is a floor signal, not a target.** Coverage exists to expose untested code. Uncovered branches in money, auth, and data-loss paths are closed first; a coverage percentage is never reported as proof of quality on its own.
9. **QA-009 — The suite must be able to fail.** Mutating one assertion's expected value in a core module — or running a mutation-testing sample on core modules — must turn the suite red; a suite that stays green under mutation is reopened as a defect.
10. **QA-010 — Flaky unit tests are defects, not weather.** A test that passes on re-run without a code change is quarantined with an owner and expiry date, or fixed; silent retries that launder intermittency into green are not permitted at this layer.

## BAN list

- **BAN-QA-001 — Assertion-free coverage gaming.** Banned: a test that executes the code under test and asserts nothing (or only that no exception was thrown) while counting toward logic coverage. Defeats: DET-CODE-012. Instead: assert the exact expected total for named inputs, e.g. `expect(cart.total()).toBe(4200)`. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-002 — Doubling the unit under test.** Banned: mocking or stubbing the module being tested, or a hand-written fake of the project's own logic, so the test verifies the double's canned answers. Defeats: DET-FAKE-008. Instead: run the real unit; double only the external index client at the boundary. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-003 — Tautological fixture assertion.** Banned: asserting that the code returns the same hardcoded constant the implementation itself contains, so test and code can be wrong together. Defeats: DET-FAKE-014. Instead: compute the expectation independently in the test (from the rule or a worked example) and assert against that. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-004 — Disabling a failing test to go green.** Banned: `.skip`, `xit`, commented-out assertions, or a deleted test used to make the suite pass without a fix or a tracked quarantine (owner + expiry, per QA-010). Defeats: DET-FAKE-022. Instead: fix the code or the test; if neither is possible now, quarantine it as a tracked defect with an owner and expiry date, and report the suite as carrying a known failure. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-QA-001 — Seeded-fault (mutation) gate.** Verifies: QA-002, QA-009. Check: in CI, run `scripts/mutation-spotcheck.sh` — it flips one expected value in a core-module test (or runs the mutation sample), runs the unit suite, and requires a non-zero exit; it then restores the file and requires exit 0. Pass: suite exits non-zero under mutation and 0 after restore. Fail: block merge; the hollow test is a defect.
- **G-QA-002 — Isolation and shuffle gate.** Verifies: QA-003. Check: CI runs the suite twice — `npm test -- --sequence.shuffle` (Vitest) / `pytest -p no:cacheprovider --random-order` equivalent for the stack — and once per test file in isolation; all runs must exit 0. Pass: every run exits 0. Fail: block merge; the order-dependent test is fixed, not re-run until green.
- **G-QA-003 — Assertion-presence gate.** Verifies: QA-002. Check: CI runs `scripts/check-assertions.sh`, which scans unit test files and exits 1 if any test body contains no assertion call (`expect(`, `assert`, `should`) and is not labeled `smoke`. Pass: script exits 0. Fail: block merge until each flagged test asserts a specific value or is relabeled smoke.
- **G-QA-004 — Wall-time budget gate.** Verifies: QA-001. Check: the CI unit job declares a timeout equal to the budget in TESTING.md (config inspection: `grep -n "timeout" .github/workflows/*.yml` shows the value); the platform kills and fails the job on breach. Pass: timeout present and the job completes inside it. Fail: block merge; slow tests are profiled and pushed down or fixed, never absorbed by raising the timeout without a TESTING.md change.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Every test asserts a specific expected value, or is labeled smoke (QA-002).
- [ ] Suite passes shuffled and with each test file run alone (QA-003, G-QA-002).
- [ ] No real network, database, filesystem, or wall-clock access in any unit test (QA-004).
- [ ] Doubles exist only at external boundaries; the unit under test runs for real (QA-006).
- [ ] Any bug fixed in this change has its failing test in the same commit (QA-007).
- [ ] Seeded-fault gate ran and the suite went red under mutation (G-QA-001).
- [ ] No skipped or disabled tests without a tracked owner and expiry date (QA-010).

# visual-regression

## Metadata

- **Owner department:** D8 QA & Testing (QA)
- **Skill version:** 1.0.0
- **Last verified:** 2026-11-21
- **Depends on:** test-strategy, browser-verification
- **Feeds into:** qa-gates

## When to use / Do NOT use

- **Use when:** a project has pages or component states where layout is the product — marketing pages, dashboards, checkout, email-critical screens — and layout drift must fail a pull request mechanically.
- **Do NOT use when:** the check is behavioral rather than visual (use e2e-testing or browser-verification), or the surface is a native app or canvas game with no stable rendered layout (use manual review and record why in TESTING.md).

## Rules

1. **QA-081 — Pinned environment.** Baselines are generated and compared inside one pinned environment — same container image, browser build, and font set — and the image digest and browser version are recorded in the test config. A baseline produced on a developer machine is invalid.
2. **QA-082 — Baselines change only by reviewed PR.** A baseline file changes only in a pull request whose description names the intentional design change it accepts. Regenerating baselines inside a feature PR without that statement is a process violation, however green it makes the run.
3. **QA-083 — Coverage by inventory.** Every template in the page/state inventory carries at least three screenshots: default, empty, and error state. The inventory comes from the design system, not from which pages someone remembered.
4. **QA-084 — Mask dynamics, never widen tolerance.** Timestamps, avatars, ads, and other dynamic regions are masked in the test that captures them. The global pixel threshold stays at the small value set in TESTING.md; raising it requires a waiver recorded per qa-gates.
5. **QA-085 — Animations frozen.** Screenshot tests run with animations disabled (`animations: "disabled"` in the screenshot assertion), so motion can never become flake.
6. **QA-086 — Diff artifact before re-run.** A failing comparison uploads the expected, actual, and diff images as CI artifacts. Triage opens the diff image first; re-running the job before reading the diff is not triage.
7. **QA-087 — Viewports match the support matrix.** The screenshot set covers every viewport class in the project's support matrix, including one mobile width; a desktop-only suite is reported as desktop-only coverage.
8. **QA-088 — Seeded-change negative control.** On a schedule, a throwaway branch shifts a header by 20px and the visual job must fail with a diff artifact. A job that passes the seeded change is itself a defect and blocks release until fixed.
9. **QA-089 — Baseline-drift report per release.** Each release produces a count of baselines changed since the previous release tag. Mass changes with no matching design-change statement block the release.
10. **QA-090 — Environment changes are single events.** A font or browser-version upgrade is one deliberate, repo-wide baseline regeneration in its own PR — never a per-test fix scattered across feature PRs.
11. **QA-091 — Compare the built artifact.** Comparisons run in CI against the pull request's built application, with the build SHA recorded beside the results — never against a locally rendered dev server.
12. **QA-092 — Quarantine expires.** A screenshot test that flakes twice in a week is quarantined with a ticket and an expiry date, and the quarantine count is reported per release. Deleting the test or silently retrying it away is forbidden.

## BAN list

- **BAN-QA-041 — Baseline regeneration to green.** Banned: running the update-snapshots command to make a red visual run pass without a reviewed PR naming the design change. Defeats: DET-VIS-007. Instead: keep the failure, open a baseline-only PR whose description states the intentional change, and let a reviewer read the diff images. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-042 — Threshold inflation.** Banned: raising the global pixel threshold or diff ratio to absorb failures instead of masking the dynamic region causing them. Defeats: DET-VIS-001. Instead: mask the timestamp element in that one test and return the threshold to the value in TESTING.md. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-043 — Desktop-only coverage.** Banned: a visual suite whose viewports are all desktop widths while the support matrix includes mobile. Defeats: DET-VIS-038. Instead: add the mobile viewport from the support matrix to every inventory template's screenshot set. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-044 — Live-animation screenshots.** Banned: capturing screenshots while CSS animations or transitions run, so pass/fail depends on frame timing. Defeats: DET-VIS-040. Instead: set `animations: "disabled"` on the screenshot assertion so every capture is the settled frame. Severity: BLOCK.
- **BAN-QA-045 — Default-state-only coverage.** Banned: screenshotting only the populated default state of a template, with no empty or error state. Defeats: DET-VIS-032. Instead: add the empty and error states from the inventory to the screenshot set before merging the template. Severity: BLOCK.

## Gates

- **G-QA-041 — Visual suite exit code.** Verifies: QA-081, QA-083, QA-085, QA-087. Check: `npx playwright test --grep @visual` in the pinned CI image. Pass: exit code 0 and the run report lists every inventory template with its default, empty, and error screenshots. Fail: block merge.
- **G-QA-042 — Seeded-change control.** Verifies: QA-088. Check: the scheduled job applies a 20px header shift on a throwaway branch, runs `npx playwright test --grep @visual`, and asserts a non-zero exit plus a diff image in the artifacts. Pass: job fails as designed and the artifact exists. Fail: block release; the visual suite is treated as non-functional.
- **G-QA-043 — Baseline-drift gate.** Verifies: QA-082, QA-089. Check: `git diff --name-only <last-release-tag>..HEAD -- '*-snapshots'` counts changed baselines; the release checklist requires a design-change statement for the count. Pass: every changed baseline traces to a reviewed baseline PR. Fail: block release.
- **G-QA-044 — Threshold config audit.** Verifies: QA-084. Check: `grep -Rn "maxDiffPixelRatio" --include="*.ts" .` and compare each value against the cap in TESTING.md. Pass: no value exceeds the cap and no per-test threshold overrides exist without a waiver reference. Fail: block merge.
[check condensed — full procedure in the source skill]

## Checklist

- [ ] Baselines were generated inside the pinned CI image, with its digest recorded (QA-081).
- [ ] Every baseline change sits in a reviewed PR naming the intentional design change (QA-082).
- [ ] Default, empty, and error states exist for every inventory template (QA-083).
- [ ] Dynamic regions are masked and the global threshold matches TESTING.md (QA-084).
- [ ] Animations are disabled in every screenshot assertion (QA-085).
- [ ] The latest seeded-change control failed the job and produced a diff artifact (QA-088).
- [ ] The release baseline-drift count is produced and explained (QA-089).
- [ ] No quarantined visual test is past its expiry date (QA-092).
